title.narrative: To reduce the average malaria prevalence in children <5yrs to <3.5% and to reduce malaria transmission to less than 1000, all by 2025. To achieve Universal Health Coverage by 2030. - Tanzania (United Republic) (01-Jan-2021-31-Dec-2023)

description.narrative: Tanzania (United Republic), Malaria, Ministry of Finance of the United Republic of Tanzania (MoF)This program has the following goals: The national goal is to reduce the average malaria prevalence in children aged less than 5 years (pfpr6-59 months) from 7% in 2017 to less than 3.5% in 2025. To reduce malaria transmission from the Annual Parasite Incidence (API) of an average of 121 per 1000 in 2019, to less than 30 per 1000 in 2025. To achieve Universal Health Coverage and reaching the targets for health related Sustainable Development Goals by 2030. The objectives of this program are: To strengthen health product management systems to ensure uninterrupted provision of health commodities. To provide integrated models of health service delivery that ensure linkages between health and community systems to improve quality, access and equitable health services. To strengthen laboratory supply chain and quality management systems to ensure availability and provision of quality services at all levels. To strengthen data systems by digitalizing and integrating data platforms to support better service delivery and outcomes for individuals and communities. Increase proportion of population with fever who seek advice/ treatment from 75% in 2017 to 81% in 2023 through strengthening an enabling environment where individuals at risk from malaria are empowered to protect themselves and their families from malaria and seek proper and timely malaria-treatment. Increase proportion of malaria control inteventions implemented annually from 63% in 2020 to 75% in 2023 by strengthening efficiency and effective coordination of malaria implementation strategies via accountable partnership.. To strengthen data systems by digitalising and integrating data platforms to support better service delivery and outcomes for individuals and communities. To strengthen coherence between national health sector and subsectoral strategies by aligning implementation and resources. To promote effective systems that is responsive to the community needs and which can compliment and link with formal health system.
